sn44.11:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccana was dwelling at Ñatika in the Brick Hall.
sn44.11:1.2: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccana and exchanged greetings with him.
sn44.11:1.3: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn44.11:1.4: “How is it, Master Kaccana, does the Tathagata exist after death?”
sn44.11:3.13: is the cause and reason why this has not been declared by the Blessed One?”
sn44.11:3.14: “Vaccha, as to the cause and condition for describing him as ‘consisting of form’ or as ‘formless’ or as ‘percipient’ or as ‘nonpercipient’ or as ‘neither percipient nor nonpercipient’: if that cause and condition were to cease completely and totally without remainder,
sn44.11:3.15: in what way could one describe him as ‘consisting of form’ or as ‘formless’ or as ‘percipient’ or as ‘nonpercipient’ or as ‘neither percipient nor nonpercipient’?”
sn44.11:3.16: “How long has it been since you went forth, Master Kaccana?”
sn44.11:3.18: “One, friend, who has gotten so much in such a time has indeed gotten much, not to speak of one who has surpassed this!”
sn44.11:5.7: The Book of the Six Sense Bases is finished.
